name: Ashen Lexicon
description: Ashen Lexicon is a small, fading world whose surface tells the story of slow decline. Pale grey dust seas spread across what were once ocean basins, their former shorelines still visible as faint mineral tide-marks on the surrounding rock. An enormous meteor crater dominates the northern hemisphere, its rim eroded to gentle hills that barely hint at the cataclysm that may have begun this world's long desiccation.

The thin atmosphere carries sound poorly, lending the planet an oppressive silence broken only by the hiss of wind-driven dust against exposed rock. At midday the sky is a washed-out violet, deepening to near-black at the horizons where the atmosphere thins to nothing. Temperature swings between day and night are severe, and the dust seas shift and resettle with each thermal cycle, slowly erasing any marks left upon them.

A mining consortium operated here for three decades before the veins ran thin and the operation was abandoned. Their complex still stands on the crater rim, its structures remarkably preserved by the dry, nearly sterile conditions. Microbial colonies were discovered in the deepest mine shafts, clinging to moisture seeping from ancient aquifers—the last living remnants of whatever biosphere once flourished here.

The microbes of Ashen Lexicon are genetically unlike anything in known databases, suggesting an independent origin of life that makes them invaluable to astrobiologists. However, the mining operation's chemical residue is slowly contaminating the aquifers that sustain them. A small preservation effort has been proposed but lacks funding, and each year the microbial colonies shrink further. The lexicon of this world's biological history is losing its final pages.
